=== FINDINGS FROM google_gemini-3_1-flash-lite ===
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: Step 0 (Session preflight) and Zombie-checker cleanup section | severity=BLOCKER | confidence=[5]
  PROBLEM: The new bullet point for issue-mode cleanup is positioned as a child of Step 0 (Session preflight), but the text instructs the session to run it only "once step 1 has read the plan" to obtain the source issue identifier.
  WHY: An unattended session following the documented step order will attempt to process cleanup logic at the end of Step 0, before Step 1 has executed its "Read it in full" step to resolve the plan and its Source issue identifier. The cleanup predicate will therefore fail to find the identifier, skip the label check, and fail to archive the stopped stage session, re-introducing the bug this PR aims to fix.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: Zombie-checker cleanup section (new issue-mode sub-bullet) | severity=MAJOR | confidence=[4]
  PROBLEM: The cleanup and rename sequences do not define robust error handling for transient failures of `set_session_title` or `mcp__github__issue_read`.
  WHY: A transient rename failure leaves the stopped session with its pre-stop title (which the cleanup does not match), and a label-read failure can cause the cleanup to skip archival without surfacing an error, leaving idle sessions visible in the session list after the issue resumes.
Requirement: The lint check (`tests/inventory_parity.py`) must pass for the PR to merge; `scripts/claude_pr_sweep.py` must be documented in the `docs/INVENTORY.md` Scripts section or explicitly exempted in `tests/inventory_exemptions.txt`.
Expected change site: `docs/INVENTORY.md` (Scripts section) or `tests/inventory_exemptions.txt`
Evidence of absence: The PR diff does not touch `docs/INVENTORY.md` to include `scripts/claude_pr_sweep.py`; `tests/inventory_parity.py` fails on this PR head with "FAIL: scripts/claude_pr_sweep.py referenced by agents.md:903 but not in docs/INVENTORY.md", blocking the merge.
SEVERITY: BLOCKER
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
Requirement: When an issue-mode `/implement-plan-claude` project stops (`Status: BLOCKED`), the stage session that stopped stays open after a human answers on the issue and comments `/reclarify`. It then has to be archived by hand. The fix's contract is that the cleanup actually fires on `/reclarify` resume, after Step 1 reads the plan and the `Source issue:` identifier is available.
Expected change site: .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md Step 1 (after "Read" in full) and the Zombie-checker cleanup section header.
Evidence of absence: No diff hunk places the issue-mode cleanup trigger inside Step 1 or appends an operational hook at the end of Step 1 to invoke the cleanup. The cleanup-section header (line 187) incorrectly assigns it to Step 0, and the new Step 0 child bullet acknowledges the dependency ("once step 1 has read the plan") but provides no runtime mechanism that fires the cleanup after Step 1 has parsed the plan.
SEVERITY: BLOCKER
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
Requirement: A contract test must pin the issue-mode cleanup trigger's placement after Step 1 reads the plan and verify the cleanup-section header distinguishes issue-mode timing, so a future edit cannot silently regress the trigger.
Expected change site: tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py
Evidence of absence: `test_issue_mode_archives_stopped_stage_sessions` (lines 245-264) only checks text-string existence. It does not assert that Step 1 references the cleanup, does not assert the cleanup-section header distinguishes issue-mode timing, and does not pin the deferred trigger's placement outside the strict step-0-cleanup invariant.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 4

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
- tests/test_implement_plan_claude_command.py: lines 260-264, the `step1 = text[text.index("1. **Resolve the plan doc.**"):text.index("2. **Pick the mode")]` slice and trigger-text assertion | severity=NIT | confidence=[3]
  PROBLEM: The contract test only pins that the "Issue-mode resume cleanup" trigger text appears somewhere inside Step 1's body; it does not pin the trigger is positioned AFTER the "Read it in full" instruction that produces the `Source issue:` line the cleanup predicate depends on. A future edit that moves the trigger to the beginning of Step 1 (before the plan read) would still satisfy the slice check, but at runtime the cleanup would run without the `Source issue:` identifier and silently skip archival — re-introducing the bug the PR is meant to fix.
  WHY: the slice bounds are coarse (start = Step 1 heading, end = Step 2 heading), so any in-Step-1 placement passes. The runtime behavior depends on the trigger being evaluated AFTER Step 1 reads the plan and parses its header. A regression that pushes the trigger above the "Read" step would pass CI and break the production cleanup on every `/reclarify` resume.
- .claude/commands/implement-plan-claude.md: line 12, the new Step 0 child bullet "**Issue-mode resume without a `— resume.` block**" | severity=NIT | confidence=[2]
  PROBLEM: The Step 0 bullet is parenthesized under Step 0 (Session preflight) yet instructs the session to "run the [Zombie-checker cleanup] too" gated on Step 1 having read the plan. The operational trigger is in Step 1, but the Step 0 bullet still reads as an action to take in Step 0. An LLM following the Step 0 bullets in order may attempt the cleanup without the `Source issue:` identifier (the cleanup predicate reads `Source issue:` from the plan header), fall through silently, and leave the stopped session unarchived.
  WHY: The bullet's text "once step 1 has read the plan, run the cleanup" is descriptive, but its placement as a Step 0 child invites a session to act on it before Step 1 has read. Step 1's "Issue-mode resume cleanup:" trigger is the operational mechanism, but the Step 0 placement remains ambiguous.
